logline: A terminally ill woman travels back in time to rewrite her past, this time letting her cheating husband and best friend have each other while she builds a better life.

bollymeter.basis: Confident genre execution and Park Min-young's performance earn it; structural drop after episode 12 and a tacked-on antagonist arc hold it off the top rung.

seasons.review_body: Marry My Husband works because it commits fully to its premise: this is revenge melodrama dressed as time-travel romance, and it never pretends otherwise. Park Min-young plays the lead with the mix of wounded resolve and darkly comic satisfaction the material demands. The first eleven episodes maintain tonal confidence, the villains are satisfyingly hateable, and the twist-to-satisfaction ratio stays high. Reviewers across MyDramaList and trade outlets noted a structural gear-change around episode twelve, where new antagonists arrive and the plotting feels retrofitted rather than planned. NME called it deliciously melodramatic and immensely addictive in a four-star review. The IMDb audience lands at 7.8, which is honest for a drama that fires on its own genre terms without transcending them.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Marry My Husband Season 1 Episode 1 aired January 1, 2024 on tvN as the premiere of the limited series NME called 'deliciously melodramatic and immensely addictive' in a four-star review. IMDb audiences scored the series 7.8. The premiere executes its premise - a terminally ill woman travels back in time with foreknowledge of every betrayal she has suffered - with tonal confidence. The dark comedy of Ji Won-hee's situation, the pleasure she takes in planning retribution, and the genuinely cruel specifics of her original life are all established in a single episode. Park Min-young grounds the show's more outlandish revisions. The premise's appeal is immediate and the episode makes it feel earned by making the betrayals specific rather than symbolic.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Ji Won-hee discovers her husband's affair and her best friend's betrayal on the same day she receives a terminal diagnosis, then immediately time-travels back to her 20s with full knowledge of what she survived. The premise is brutal and the episode delivers it without flinching, establishing the show's darkly comic tone in the gap between how awful Ji Won-hee's original life was and how much pleasure she takes in planning otherwise.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ji Won-hee's first deliberate act after returning to the past - a small revenge that tells the audience exactly what kind of show this will be.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 5
episode_reviews.review_body: Marry My Husband Season 1 Episode 5 aired January 8, 2024 on tvN as the fifth episode of the limited series NME scored four stars, calling it 'deliciously melodramatic and immensely addictive.' IMDb audiences landed the series at 7.8. The episode deploys the show's core engine in its most confident form: Ji Won-hee actively engineers the conditions for her cheating best friend to meet her cheating husband, a manipulation the show frames as comedic rather than bitter. The villain duo are at their most entertainingly hateable, and the tonal balance between dark wish-fulfillment and genuine character work is at its most stable. Episodes one through eleven were broadly praised before reviewers noted a structural gear-change with new antagonists around episode twelve.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Ji Won-hee actively engineers the conditions for her cheating best friend to meet her cheating husband, and the episode makes this manipulation comedic rather than bitter. The villain duo are at their most entertainingly hateable here, and the show is running at full confidence.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The moment Ji Won-hee's setup works exactly as she planned - the show's thesis that the premise permits satisfaction without apology.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 10
episode_reviews.review_body: Marry My Husband Season 1 Episode 10 aired February 6, 2024 on tvN as the tenth of sixteen episodes. NME's four-star review called the series 'deliciously melodramatic and immensely addictive.' The 7.8 IMDb score reflects an audience that found the show's genre execution confident within its stated limits. Episode 10 marks the transition just before the structural gear-change reviewers noted around episode twelve: the romantic arc between Ji Won-hee and Min-hwan is entering a more earnest register, the tonal confidence of the revenge-comedy first half carries over, and the late-arriving antagonist subplot has not yet arrived. As a midpoint episode, it represents the show in its most balanced state.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The show pivots toward its romantic arc with Min-hwan as a genuine love interest rather than a plot tool, and the tonal confidence of the first half carries over cleanly. This is the episode just before the structural gear-change around episode twelve.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Min-hwan recognising that Ji Won-hee is not acting the way a person in her position should act - and deciding he wants to understand why.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 16
episode_reviews.review_body: Marry My Husband Season 1 Episode 16 aired February 20, 2024 on tvN as the finale of the limited series NME called 'deliciously melodramatic and immensely addictive.' IMDb audiences scored the series 7.8. Critics noted the late-arriving antagonist subplot introduced around episode twelve required more patience than it earned, but broadly agreed the finale delivered on the romantic promise made from episode one. Park Min-young's performance carries the emotional register through the closing sequence. The show's essential argument - that a woman who was failed by her closest relationships deserves to rebuild from scratch with full knowledge - is resolved in terms the 16-episode investment validates.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale satisfies on the romantic terms the show promised from episode one, even if the late-arriving antagonist subplot requires more patience than it earns. The ending puts Ji Won-hee exactly where she deserved to be, and Park Min-young plays the relief with enough restraint to make it feel earned rather than simply delivered.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Ji Won-hee in the life she built - the image the show spent sixteen episodes working toward.
